LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Meta.Meta__Description: The Layout Editor's vector tools: Circle and Arc, which draw, and Trim, Extend, Join, Split, Offset, Fillet and Chamfer, which edit what is already on the sheet. What every one of them makes is an ordinary vector - a run of paper points in Sheet__Shapes - so select, move, copy, fill, hatch, dash, the eyedropper, a floor area, the PDF and the web viewer all work on the result with nothing to learn. The keys are in Na__Hotkeys__DrawingTabs__.json with every other drawing-tab key; this file holds how the tools behave and every word they put on the screen.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Meta.Meta__Research: SketchUp LayOut 2026 help (Using Drafting Tools, Splitting and Joining, Offsetting, Creating Arcs, Drawing a Circle or Ellipse, Shaping Polygons, Grouping Entities), the LayOut 2026 Quick Reference Card and release notes, the SketchUp forums, AutoCAD 2026 help (TRIM, EXTEND, TRIMEXTENDMODE) and Adam's own LayOut 2026 keymap (layout.private.json), researched 21-Sep-2026. COPIED FROM LAYOUT: Trim and Extend have no 'pick the cutting edge first' step - hover the piece, see what will happen, click (LayOut 2026's Trim and Extend work as AutoCAD's Quick mode does); the FENCE - click on bare paper, draw a line through several lines, click again, and every one of them is trimmed or extended; Join by clicking one piece then the next, the result taking the FIRST piece's style, and Join run on a selection joining everything in it at once (LayOut 2025); ends must MEET to be joined; Split where the line is clicked, an intersection of two lines splitting both; Offset by click, preview, click, with a typed distance; Fillet's radius and Chamfer's single distance (an equal cut, 45 degrees across a right angle) typed into the Measurements box; Circle by centre then radius with a typed radius, 'd' for a diameter and '6s' for sides (LayOut's Polygon tool is the same gesture, so the two are one tool here); the Arc tool's four ways of drawing - 2 Point (start, end, bulge), Arc (centre, start, end), 3 Point, and Pie - with a typed bulge, radius or angle; the drawing tools working INSIDE an open group and drawing into it. COPIED FROM AUTOCAD: Shift swaps Trim and Extend for as long as it is held; the span to be removed is shown before the click; every vector is a cutting edge. NOT COPIED, DELIBERATELY: AutoCAD's Quick mode DELETES an object that crosses nothing - here nothing happens and a line above the Measurements box says why, because a stray click should never cost a line. LayOut's curves are Beziers; here a circle or an arc is a run of short edges, as SketchUp's are, counted from its radius on paper so the flats stand no more than ChordToleranceMm off the true curve - the painters round every joint, so it prints as a curve - which keeps every reader of a vector unchanged. LayOut refuses to offset inside a group; here it works there. BEYOND BOTH: Trim and Extend can stop at the DRAWING'S OWN LINEWORK under the sheet (CutToDrawing), which neither LayOut nor AutoCAD can do with a referenced model; a fillet or chamfer size of nothing makes two lines simply meet (AutoCAD's radius 0); Join can bridge ends that do not meet (Illustrator's Join) when JoinBridges is on. KEYS: T is the Text tool on the sheet, as it is in LayOut, so Trim takes T only while a container is open - where the Text tool could not be used anyway - and Shift held with Extend (Shift+T) trims from anywhere; LayOut's own Trim is Shift+T and its Extend Shift+E.

LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Behaviour.Behaviour__Description: How the tools behave. Sizes are paper millimetres unless they say otherwise.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Behaviour.Behaviour__ChordToleranceMmNote: How far the flat of a circle's or an arc's edge may stand off the true curve, on paper. A hundredth of a millimetre is a fifth of the finest pen: a 15 mm circle gets 88 edges, a 100 mm one 224.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Behaviour.Behaviour__SegmentsNote: The fewest and the most edges a whole circle is given when the count is Auto. 24 is SketchUp's own circle. A count typed by hand (6s) is used as typed, from 3 up.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Behaviour.Behaviour__JoinToleranceMmNote: How close two ends must be to count as meeting. Ends snapped together meet exactly; this forgives ends placed by eye that look joined at any sensible zoom - half the finest pen's width.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Behaviour.Behaviour__HalfCircleSnapPxNote: A 2 Point Arc whose bulge comes within this many screen pixels of half its chord lands on the exact half circle, as SketchUp's does.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Behaviour.Behaviour__MaxExtendMmNote: The furthest an end may be carried on to reach a line: further than the largest sheet is across, so in practice only a guard against a runaway.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Behaviour.Behaviour__DrawInsideOpenGroupNote: True is LayOut's behaviour: while a GROUP is open for editing, the Draw, Rectangle, Circle and Arc tools leave it open and what they draw joins it. False is how the editor behaved before the vector tools: picking any drawing tool closed the container and drew on the sheet.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Behaviour.Behaviour__ShiftSwapsNote: True is AutoCAD's: holding Shift with Trim up extends, and with Extend up trims, for as long as it is held.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Behaviour.Behaviour__CutToOwnCrossingsNote: A path that crosses itself can be trimmed at the crossing, and an end can be extended on to its own path.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Behaviour.Behaviour__DefaultsNote: What the panel starts with in a browser that has never used the tools. circleSegments 0 is Auto. The three sizes are AS TYPED: real millimetres at the drawing's scale while Draw at scale is ticked in the Vectors panel, paper millimetres while it is not.

LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Preview.Preview__Description: The colours and weights of what the tools show before a click. Screen pixels, whatever the zoom.

LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__Description: Every word the vector tools put on the screen.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__ToolDrawTitle: Line (L): click points, click the first point again to close, Enter or a double click to finish.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__ToolRectangleTitle: Rectangle (R): click one corner then the opposite one, or drag. Type width x height.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__ToolCircleTitle: Circle (C): click the centre, then the radius - or drag from one to the other. Type a radius (1500), a diameter (3000d) or a number of sides (6s) and press Enter; typed straight after it lands, it resizes that circle.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__ToolArcTitle: Arc (Shift+A): as set below - 2 Point draws start, end, then the bulge. Type the bulge, or a radius (750r), and press Enter.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__ToolTrimTitle: Trim (T while editing inside a group or a vector; or hold Shift with Extend): hover a line and the piece that will go shows red - click to remove it back to the nearest lines crossing it. Click bare paper, draw a line across several and click again to trim them all. Hold Shift to extend instead.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__ToolExtendTitle: Extend (Shift+T): hover near the end of a line and where it will run on to shows blue - click to extend it to the next line in its way. Click bare paper, draw a line across several and click again to extend them all. Hold Shift to trim instead.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__ToolJoinTitle: Join (J): click one line, then each line that meets its end - they become one vector with the first one's style, and it closes into a shape when the last end meets the first. With several vectors selected, J joins everything that meets at once.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__ToolSplitTitle: Split (U): click a line to cut it in two there. Where two lines cross, one click cuts both.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__ToolOffsetTitle: Offset (F): click a line or a shape, move to the side the copy goes and click - or type how far and press Enter.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__ToolFilletTitle: Fillet (Shift+F): click a corner to round it, or click one line then another to round the corner they make and join them. Type the radius and press Enter; a radius of 0 makes two lines simply meet.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__ToolChamferTitle: Chamfer (Shift+C): click a corner to cut it off, or click one line then another. Type the distance back from the corner and press Enter.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__OptionSegmentsTitle: How many straight edges a circle or an arc is drawn with. Auto gives as many as its size on paper needs to print as a true curve. A number draws exactly that many, so 6 is a hexagon; typing 6s while drawing sets it too.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__OptionCutToDrawingTitle: On: Trim and Extend stop at the lines of the drawings under the sheet as well as at the sheet's own vectors - trim a line back to a wall, run one on to the ground line. Off: only vectors cut vectors, as in LayOut.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__OptionJoinBridges: Bridge ends that do not meet
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__OptionJoinBridgesTitle: On: Join links the two nearest ends with a straight edge however far apart they are. Off: ends must meet, as in LayOut.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__OptionSizeTitle: As typed into the Measurements box: real millimetres at the drawing's scale while Draw at scale is ticked, paper millimetres while it is not.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__CurveRadiusTitle: The radius of the selected circle or arc, at the scale the Measurements box is working at. Change it and the curve is redrawn about the same centre.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__CurveSidesTitle: How many edges the selected curve is drawn with. 0 gives it as many as its size needs.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__MeasureTitleCircle: Type a radius and press Enter - 1500, or 1.5m. 3000d is a diameter, 6s is six sides and 0s is as many sides as it needs. Typed straight after a circle lands, it resizes that circle.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__MeasureTitleArc: Type the bulge and press Enter, or a radius as 750r. With the arc drawn from its centre, type the radius, then the angle in degrees.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__MeasureTitleSize: Type the size and press Enter - 150, or 0.15m. It is remembered for the next one.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__HintCircleRadius: Circle: click the radius, or type it.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__HintArcBulge: Arc: move off the line and click, or type the bulge.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__HintArcFrom: Arc: click where it starts - that sets the radius.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__HintArcSweep: Arc: go round and click where it ends, or type the angle.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__HintArcThrough: Arc: click a point it passes through.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__HintTrim: Trim: click the piece to remove. Shift extends.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__HintExtend: Extend: click near the end to run on. Shift trims.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__HintFence: Draw across the lines, then click again.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__HintJoinNext: Join: click a line that meets its end. Esc finishes.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__HintOffsetPick: Offset: click a line or a shape.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__HintOffsetPlace: Offset: click the side, or type how far.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__HintCornerFirst: Click a corner, or the first of two lines.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__SayNothingCrosses: Nothing crosses that line, so there is nothing to trim it back to.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__SayNothingAhead: There is no line ahead of that end to extend it to.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__SayClosedNoEnd: A closed shape has no end to extend. Split it first.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__SayLocked: That vector is on a locked layer.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__SayNotVector: Only plain vectors can be edited this way - not pictures, QR codes or measured rooms.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__SayEndsApart: Those ends do not meet. Snap them together, or tick Bridge ends that do not meet.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__SayClosedNoJoin: A closed shape has no free end to join.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__SayJoinedClosed: Joined and closed: it can now take a fill.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__SayNothingJoins: None of the selected vectors meet end to end.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__SaySplitEnd: That is the end of the line: there is nothing to part.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__SayCornerStraight: There is no corner there to work on.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__SayCornerLong: That size is too big for the edges at that corner.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__SayCornerEnds: Click the END edge of each line - the corner is made where those two would meet.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__SayCornerParallel: Those two lines are parallel: they make no corner.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__SayOffsetGone: Offset that far, nothing of the shape is left.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__SaySegmentsAuto: Circles and arcs: as many sides as they need.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__SayRadiusSmall: That radius is too small to reach between the two ends.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__SayNeedPoint: Click a point first, then type.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__SayBadValue: Not a size. Type 1500, 1.5m, 3000d for a diameter, 750r for a radius or 6s for sides.
LayoutEditor__VectorTools__Labels.Labels__SayBadAngle: Not an angle. Type degrees, such as 90.
